guide.title: Guide
guide.p1: Use the New Tab page or the File menu: Open (Ctrl+O) an existing folder, Clone (Ctrl+N) from a URL or a hosting service, Create (Ctrl+I) a new repository with a .gitignore and a licence.
guide.p2: Each row is a commit. Coloured lines are branches; the labels on the left are branches and tags (the laptop icon means local, the cloud means remote). Click a row to see its files, click a file to see the diff. Up and Down move the selection.
guide.p3: When files change, a // WIP row appears at the top. Click it, stage files (or Stage all changes), write a summary and press Commit. Undo takes the last commit back with its changes kept.
guide.p4: Pull downloads and merges the remote branch (the arrow next to it offers fetch, fast-forward only and rebase). Push uploads your branch and sets its upstream the first time.
guide.p5: Branch creates a branch at the selected commit. Double-click a branch to check it out; right-click for merge, rename and delete. Stash puts your changes aside, Pop brings them back.
guide.p6: In Preferences > AI choose an API (Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible, Ollama) or an ACP agent such as Claude Code or Gemini CLI. Then use the AI button, the Agents tab or right-click a commit to ask for an explanation, a review or a commit message.
guide.p7: GitCerberoCraft has a built-in Git engine. For credential managers, Git LFS and rebase you can download the official Git from Preferences > Git, choosing the version.
guide.p8: Every .json file in a lang folder is a language. Copy en.json, rename it (for example fr.json), translate the texts and change language.name: the app finds it by itself within a couple of seconds.
guide.p9: gitcerberocraft-cli runs status, fetch, pull, push, commit and more from a terminal. 'gitcerberocraft-cli mcp' starts an MCP server so AI agents can use the same Git actions. Preferences > MCP shows a ready-to-paste configuration.

auth.no_token: No token saved. Add one in Preferences > Integrations.
auth.token_invalid: The saved token was refused (401): it is wrong, expired or revoked. Create a new one and paste it in Preferences > Integrations.
auth.token_ok_classic: Token works: signed in as {0}. Scopes: {1}
auth.no_token_github: No GitHub token is saved, so Git used the system credential manager. Paste a token in Preferences > Integrations (classic token with the 'repo' scope, or a fine-grained token with 'Contents: Read and write').
auth.no_token_gitlab: No GitLab token is saved. Paste one in Preferences > Integrations (scope 'write_repository').
auth.no_write: The token belongs to '{0}', which cannot write to {1}. Use a token of the account that owns the repository, or ask the owner to add '{0}' as a collaborator (or push to your fork).
auth.missing_scope: The token of '{0}' is a classic token without the 'repo' scope (it has: {1}). Edit it on GitHub > Settings > Developer settings > Tokens and tick 'repo'.
auth.workflow_scope: The push changes files in .github/workflows: the token also needs the 'workflow' scope.
auth.fine_grained: The token of '{0}' is a fine-grained token: on GitHub > Settings > Developer settings > Fine-grained tokens, make sure it includes the repository {1} and has 'Contents: Read and write'. Tokens for an organisation may also need the organisation's approval.
auth.repo_hidden: The token of '{0}' cannot see {1}: the repository is not included in the token, or the account has no access to it.
auth.sso: The organisation uses single sign-on: authorise the token for it on GitHub (Configure SSO next to the token). {0}
auth.looks_ok: The token of '{0}' has write access. If it still fails, check the branch protection rules of the repository.
auth.gitlab_scope: Signed in as '{0}'. Check that the token has the 'write_repository' scope and that '{0}' has at least the Developer role in {1} (protected branches may need Maintainer).
auth.ssh_remote: This remote uses SSH, so tokens are not used: check that your SSH key is added to your account, or switch the remote to its https:// address.

release.title: Release Notes
release.item1: Commit graph with branches, tags, remote branches and work in progress.
release.item2: Stage, unstage, discard and commit (with amend) from the side panel, with diffs.
release.item3: Pull (merge, fast-forward only, rebase), push, fetch and auto fetch.
release.item4: Branches, tags, stashes, cherry pick, revert, reset, undo and redo.
release.item5: AI assistant by API (Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible, Ollama) or ACP agent.
release.item6: Download Git for your system, choosing the version from the official releases.
release.item8: Command-line tool with an MCP server for AI agents.
release.item9: Built-in Git engine: works even when Git is not installed.
release.item10: Launchpad with all recent repositories and their state.
